exempt #18145 — measured 2026-09-04, and the exemption holds for a sharper reason than first recorded. The structural rule sits at (0,4,0) (`.neo-dialog.neo-panel .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button`), not (0,3,0), which puts it above 13 of the 16 background-color states a header button can win: `:hover`, `:active`, `.neo-disabled`, the ghost/secondary/tertiary variants, and those variants' own hover and disabled rules. The other 3 are not a specificity question at all — ghost/secondary/tertiary `:active` declare their background `!important` (`resources/scss/src/button/Base.scss:205,258,317`) while the structural rule here does not, so importance beats it at every weight and those three resolve to the variant active colour inside a dialog header rather than to the transparent declared above. That widens the exemption rather than narrowing it: a move would have to reproduce an importance flag as well as sixteen tokens. The neo families swallow the 13 at (0,5,0) and that is their intended flat-chrome design; the classic families swallow none, so moving the selector silently changes classic paint unless every state gets its own token — which freezes an open extension point, because a future button variant would then stop applying inside dialog headers with nothing failing. Moving the base declaration alone is the trap: it looks correct and every per-file emitted-CSS diff stays clean, because the classic regression is a cascade outcome no single file shows. `height` and `min-width` have no competing declarant and could move alone, but the file stays baselined either way, so the partial move buys nothing. CSS has no per-declaration opt-out; this needs a design decision rather than a refactor, and #18107's `:where()` weight surface is the likeliest place it gets one.
